metadata.title: Inkling 2 Small, What Changed?
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Yoruba (rotating off Irish 'Dia duit' from 2026-11-09-inkling-encoder-free). Persona is the presenter named in B01 (Ritik); channel is @HumanitariansAI. Wagwan is Bear's alone and never applies here.
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity skin throughout. Terracotta marks exactly one thing per beat: the accented row, the accented bar, or the verdict's key line. Everything else is warm ink on cream.
metadata.note: Re-cut of the researched draft onto the six proven toolkit patterns (ClaudeComposerAsk, ReelExecSummary, ReelFramework, BlipLadder, ClaudeVerdictArtifact, ClaudeTitleOutro), each with a registered 916 twin — the draft's Inkling* scene family was never built, and no new scene code was written. Structure is the PROOF arc: hook -> the config-first audit shown as a 3-step rubric (B01, before any example) -> each body beat applies one step (diff, recompute, match change to reason) -> friction -> a hard case that forces a third score (BORROWED) -> scored verdict -> a copyable task with GOOD/FLAG lines. Every number on screen carries its source in the same frame; computed figures say 'computed' and name their assumptions. Each claim beat carries a `legibility` contract (what artifact is on screen when the claim is voiced, and how it stays readable). Facts re-verified 2026-11-25 against both config.json files, both release posts, the model cards and arXiv:2603.15031. 9:16 twin emitted mechanically from the same beat list.

beats.narration: Here's a reversal. In July, Thinking Machines built Inkling with no vision encoder, on purpose. Inkling 2 Small brings one back, and drops audio. And the post doesn't say why. Let's audit what changed.
beats.narration_text: Inkling 2 Small vs Inkling: (1) diff the two config.json files field by field, (2) recompute the headline parameter counts from the config, (3) for each change, quote the lab's stated reason — or mark it OPEN.

props.source: The rubric this reel applies · run on thinkingmachines/Inkling config.json and thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small config.json

beats.legibility: The rubric is the artifact: 3 numbered cards, revealed as each step is voiced (cards land at 44/53/61% of the beat, after a 15-word intro), held to the end. Framework is complete on screen by ~23 s, before any example.

beats.narration: Step one: diff the configs. Forty-eight layers instead of sixty-six, and narrower. Three hundred eighty-four experts, eight active, none shared. A twenty-three-layer vision transformer replaces the four-layer patch network, and the audio block is gone. Plus one brand-new key.

props.heading: Inkling → Inkling 2 Small, field by field

moves.label: EXPERTS
moves.detail: 256 routed + 2 shared, 6 active → 384 routed, 8 active, 0 shared.

moves.label: INPUTS
moves.detail: 4-layer hMLP on 40px patches → 23-layer ViT on 20px. audio_config: gone.

moves.label: NEW KEY
moves.detail: n_layers_per_attn_res_block: 6. Inkling's config has no such key.

props.keepNote: Every change sits in two public files. None arrives with a reason attached.
props.source: HF config.json · thinkingmachines/Inkling config.json (Jul 15 2026) vs thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small config.json (Nov 5 2026)

beats.legibility: Old → new values side by side in each row, each with its config key as receipt; rows reveal in the order voiced and stay up for the rest of the beat (row 4 holds ≥ 6 s).

beats.narration: Step two: recompute the headline. One expert is three matrices, forty-six oh eight by twenty-three oh four: about thirty-two million parameters. Eight experts, forty-eight layers: twelve point two billion. Add attention and embeddings: seventeen point three. The lab says seventeen. It checks out.

props.heading: Active parameters per token, from config.json
props.exception: All 384 experts + MTP head + vision encoder ≈ 594.1B (lab: 594B). Tied embeddings would give 16.3B and 593.1B, so untied fits both.
props.source: Computed from thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small config.json (gated MLP: gate, up, down; router omitted) · 17B / 594B: Thinking Machines, Nov 5 2026

beats.legibility: Each multiplication is printed under its bar as the bar grows (31.9M per expert is on screen when voiced); the lab's 17B is the dashed line, on screen with the computed 17.3 for the last third of the beat.

beats.narration: Now the friction. It's called Small. Compute per token fell fifty-nine percent. Stored parameters fell only thirty-nine. And serving it still takes at least five hundred gigabytes of GPU memory. So which number earns the name Small?

props.heading: Small? Serving still needs ≥ 500 GB of GPU memory
props.exception: Each token now uses 2.9% of the stored weights, down from 4.2% — the model got sparser.
props.source: Computed from lab totals: 594B / 17B (Thinking Machines, Nov 5 2026) · 975B / 41B (Thinking Machines, Jul 15 2026) · ≥ 500 GB: HF model card (NVFP4 checkpoint)

beats.legibility: The two bars that disagree (−59% vs −39%) sit together with Inkling's 100% bar for ≥ 8 s; the 500 GB card figure is in the heading from the first second, so it is legible before it is voiced.

beats.narration: Step three: match each change to a reason. The lab says: a two hundred ninety-two million parameter vision encoder. The config shows twenty-three blocks, a thousand twenty-four wide. That lands on about two hundred ninety-two million. The what checks out. But why drop encoder-free, or audio? Not published.

props.heading: The vision encoder: claim, config, math

moves.label: LAB SAYS
moves.detail: “a 292M-parameter vision encoder based on Perception Encoder”

moves.label: WHY?
moves.detail: Not published: no reason given for dropping encoder-free, or audio.

props.keepNote: The what checks out. The why stays OPEN: the Nov 5 post has no architecture section.
props.source: Thinking Machines, Nov 5 2026 (quote) · thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small config.json vision_config · computed: 12·d² per ViT block (4d² attention + 8d² MLP)

beats.legibility: LAB SAYS and CONFIG/COMPUTED are rows 1–3 of one frame: claim and evidence side by side from ~45% of the beat to the end (≥ 9 s); the open WHY? row holds ≥ 6 s with its receipt.

beats.narration: Now a hard case. A new key: attention-residual blocks, six layers each. The lab never mentions it. The nearest paper, from the Kimi team, swaps the fixed residual sum for attention over earlier blocks. But its evidence comes from another model. So: borrowed, not checked.
beats.narration_text: Now a hard case. A new key: attention-residual blocks, six layers each. The lab never mentions it. The nearest paper, from the Kimi team, swaps the fixed residual sum for attention over earlier blocks. But its evidence comes from another model. So: borrowed, not checked.

props.heading: Attention residuals: a reason, but whose?

moves.label: LAB SAYS
moves.detail: Nothing. Neither the Nov 5 post nor the model card mentions it.

moves.label: PAPER
moves.detail: Block AttnRes: attend over earlier blocks, not a fixed sum at weight 1.

moves.label: BUT
moves.detail: Its evidence is from Kimi Linear, 48B total / 3B active — not this model.

props.keepNote: A paper's reason is not this lab's evidence. Score it BORROWED, not CHECKED.
props.source: thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small config.json · Kimi Team, Attention Residuals, arXiv:2603.15031 (Mar 2026)

beats.legibility: Config, lab silence and the paper's claim are on screen together (rows 1–3 from ~54%); the BUT row, with its arXiv receipt, holds ≥ 5 s before the BORROWED keep-note lands.

beats.narration: The verdict. The what is fully auditable: both headline numbers reproduce from the config. The why isn't. No change comes with a published reason, and the one paper we found is borrowed. What: checked. Why: open.

props.artifactHeading: Audit scorecard: what CHECKED · why OPEN
artifactLines: CHECKED — 17B active and the 292M encoder both reproduce from config.json.
VISIBLE — 48 layers, 384 unshared experts, a ViT in, audio out, AttnRes blocks.
OPEN — no published reason for any of them; AttnRes is BORROWED from a paper.
FRICTION — “Small” per token (17B active), not to host (≥ 500 GB of VRAM).
props.sourceNote: Thinking Machines (Jul 15 & Nov 5 2026) · HF config.json, Inkling + Inkling-2-Small · arXiv:2603.15031

beats.legibility: Scorecard lines name each claim with its score (CHECKED / OPEN / BORROWED); source note in the same card.

beats.narration: Your turn. Paste this with two configs from any open model family. A good answer shows every multiplication, and scores each change: quoted, open, or borrowed. Flag any reason it can't quote.
